title: Transport of twist tower and inverse evaluation equations along transition isomorphisms
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set and $\mathcal A_i$ categories [def-nagata-category]. For $i\leq j$ let $B_{ji},C_{ji}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ be functors with natural isomorphisms $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\cong C_{ji}$. Suppose $B$ has natural associators $d_{kji}:B_{kj}B_{ji}\cong B_{ki}$ and units $\lambda_i:B_{ii}\cong1$ satisfying the coherence and unit equations of [lem-pur-transition-associator-iso-transport], and let $a,u$ be its transported associators and units:
$$a_{kji,K}=\chi_{ki,K}d_{kji,K}(\chi_{kj,C_{ji}K}B_{kj}(\chi_{ji,K}))^{-1},\qquad u_{i,K}=\lambda_{i,K}\chi_{ii,K}^{-1}.$$
Composition is functional. For each integer $m$ let $T_{i,m}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_i$ be an endofunctor with a natural isomorphism $\epsilon_{i,m}:T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}\cong1$. Suppose specified natural isomorphisms $\bar\beta_{ji,m}:B_{ji}T_{i,m}\cong T_{j,m}B_{ji}$ satisfy, for every $K\in\mathcal A_i$,
$$T_{k,m}(d_{kji,K})\bar\beta_{kj,m,B_{ji}K}B_{kj}(\bar\beta_{ji,m,K})=\bar\beta_{ki,m,K}d_{kji,T_{i,m}K},$$
$$\epsilon_{j,m,B_{ji}K}T_{j,-m}(\bar\beta_{ji,m,K})\bar\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}=B_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
Define $\beta_{ji,m,K}=T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}$. These are natural isomorphisms $C_{ji}T_{i,m}\cong T_{j,m}C_{ji}$ satisfying
$$T_{k,m}(a_{kji,K})\beta_{kj,m,C_{ji}K}C_{kj}(\beta_{ji,m,K})=\beta_{ki,m,K}a_{kji,T_{i,m}K},$$
$$\epsilon_{j,m,C_{ji}K}T_{j,-m}(\beta_{ji,m,K})\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}=C_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
Their unit-normalized components are exactly
$$T_{i,m}(u_{i,K})\beta_{ii,m,K}u_{i,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}=T_{i,m}(\lambda_{i,K})\bar\beta_{ii,m,K}\lambda_{i,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}.$$
More generally, for any $i\leq j$ with $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal A_j$ and any specified natural isomorphism $\lambda:B_{ji}\cong1$, set $v_K=\lambda_K\chi_{ji,K}^{-1}$. Without identifying $T_{i,m}$ with $T_{j,m}$ one has
$$T_{j,m}(v_K)\beta_{ji,m,K}v_{T_{i,m}K}^{-1}=T_{j,m}(\lambda_K)\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\lambda_{T_{i,m}K}^{-1}.$$
Thus normalization of the transition unit retains any prescribed nonidentity ordinary twist comparison. If its ordinary normalized component is identity under specified identifications of the two twists, so is its transported component. These assertions require only the displayed data and equations; no monoidal, additive, triangulated or completeness structure is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $i\leq j,m$ and abbreviate $F=B_{ji}$, $F'=C_{ji}$, $x=\chi_{ji}$, $P=T_{i,m}$, $Q=T_{j,m}$, $b=\bar\beta_{ji,m}$ and $p_K=Q(x_K)b_Kx_{PK}^{-1}$. Each factor is invertible: for any functor $Q$, the two composites of $Q(x)$ and $Q(x^{-1})$ are identities by preservation of composition and identities. Explicitly $p_K^{-1}=x_{PK}b_K^{-1}Q(x_K^{-1})$. For $f:K\to L$, naturality of $x,b,x^{-1}$ gives
$$Q(F'f)p_K=Q(x_L)Q(Ff)b_Kx_{PK}^{-1}=Q(x_L)b_LF(Pf)x_{PK}^{-1}=p_LF'(Pf).$$
Hence these components define the asserted natural isomorphism. Here naturality means $G(f)\eta_K=\eta_LF(f)$ for $\eta:F\to G$; its inverse equation follows by multiplying this equation by the inverse components. These are definitions and cancellation in the categories of [def-nagata-category], not an additional transport theorem.

proof.text:
For the tower fix $i\leq j\leq k,m$. In addition to Step 2 put $G=B_{kj}$, $G'=C_{kj}$, $y=\chi_{kj}$, $R=T_{k,m}$, $c=\bar\beta_{kj,m}$ and $q=\beta_{kj,m}$. Then $z_K=y_{F'K}G(x_K)$ (suppressing $kji$). Naturality of $y$ at $p_K$ and the defining equation $q_Xy_{QX}=R(y_X)c_X$ give the first equality below. Use $p_Kx_{PK}=Q(x_K)b_K$ for the second and naturality of $c:GQ\to RG$ at $x_K:FK\to F'K$ for the third:
$$\begin{aligned}
q_{F'K}G'(p_K)z_{PK}&=R(y_{F'K})c_{F'K}G(p_Kx_{PK})\\
&=R(y_{F'K})c_{F'K}G(Q(x_K))G(b_K)\\
&=R(y_{F'K})R(G(x_K))c_{FK}G(b_K)\\
&=R(z_K)c_{FK}G(b_K).
\end{aligned}$$
Every map has source $GF(PK)$ and target $R(G'F'K)$. This is a direct component calculation, using no compatibility for the transported comparisons.

proof.text:
Keep Step 3's notation and put $h=\chi_{ki}$, $e=\bar\beta_{ki,m}$, $r=\beta_{ki,m}$, $d=d_{kji}$ and $a=a_{kji}$. Precompose the proposed tower equality with the isomorphism $z_{PK}$. Step 3, then $a_Kz_K=h_Kd_K$, the assumed ordinary tower equation, and $r_Kh_{PK}=R(h_K)e_K$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
R(a_K)q_{F'K}G'(p_K)z_{PK}
&=R(h_K)R(d_K)c_{FK}G(b_K)\\
&=R(h_K)e_Kd_{PK}\\
&=r_Kh_{PK}d_{PK}\\
&=r_Ka_{PK}z_{PK}.
\end{aligned}$$
Postcomposing both expressions on the right with $z_{PK}^{-1}$ proves exactly the tower equation for $\beta$. This uses the ordinary tower hypothesis at the original object $K$, not a tower hypothesis for $C$.

proof.text:
For evaluation return to Step 2's notation and set $N=T_{i,-m}$, $M=T_{j,-m}$, $c=\bar\beta_{ji,-m}$ and $q=\beta_{ji,-m}$. The component $q_{PK}$ equals $M(x_{PK})c_{PK}x_{NPK}^{-1}$. Expanding $p_K$ therefore cancels the adjacent factors $M(x_{PK}^{-1})M(x_{PK})$:
$$\epsilon_{j,m,F'K}M(p_K)q_{PK}=\epsilon_{j,m,F'K}MQ(x_K)M(b_K)c_{PK}x_{NPK}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of the specified $\epsilon_{j,m}:MQ\to1$ at $x_K:FK\to F'K$ says $\epsilon_{j,m,F'K}MQ(x_K)=x_K\epsilon_{j,m,FK}$. Thus the last display equals
$$x_K\epsilon_{j,m,FK}M(b_K)c_{PK}x_{NPK}^{-1}.$$
No symmetry between $m$ and $-m$, and no triangle identities for an adjunction, have been assumed.

proof.text:
The ordinary evaluation equation in the hypotheses identifies $\epsilon_{j,m,FK}M(b_K)c_{PK}$ from Step 5 with $F(\epsilon_{i,m,K})$. Naturality of $x:F\to F'$ at the morphism $\epsilon_{i,m,K}:NPK\to K$ now gives
$$x_KF(\epsilon_{i,m,K})x_{NPK}^{-1}=F'(\epsilon_{i,m,K})x_{NPK}x_{NPK}^{-1}=F'(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
Together with Step 5 this is the asserted transported inverse evaluation equation, for every integer $m$, including $m=0$.

proof.text:
For the general normalization clause assume $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal A_j$ and let $\lambda:F\cong1$ be the specified isomorphism. Keep $P=T_{i,m}$ and $Q=T_{j,m}$ distinct and set $v_K=\lambda_Kx_K^{-1}$. Its inverse at $PK$ is $v_{PK}^{-1}=x_{PK}\lambda_{PK}^{-1}$. Direct substitution yields
$$\begin{aligned}
Q(v_K)p_Kv_{PK}^{-1}
&=Q(\lambda_K)Q(x_K^{-1})Q(x_K)b_Kx_{PK}^{-1}x_{PK}\lambda_{PK}^{-1}\\
&=Q(\lambda_K)b_K\lambda_{PK}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides are morphisms $PK\to QK$. Thus this equality does not require $P=Q$. The identity cancels only the $x$ components and does not replace the ordinary normalized comparison by an identity.

proof.text: For self-transition normalization expand unitIso and twistIso directly. Cancel chi followed by chi inverse at T_i,m(K); functoriality and the inverse equations cancel T_i,m(chi_K) followed by T_i,m(chi inverse_K). The remaining expression is exactly lambda inverse at T_i,m(K), then the ordinary twist comparison, then T_i,m(lambda_K). This is also the specialization of Step 7 to P = Q = T_i,m. For a specified identification e : P iso Q, postcompose the equality in Step 7 with e inverse. Reassociation shows that identity of the ordinary normalized comparison implies identity of the transported comparison. No additional structure or equality P = Q is needed in that general clause.
